questions.q: How many vessels does the umbilical cord contain and what do they carry?

options.t: Two arteries and one vein, all oxygenated
options.e: Wrong. The arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the fetus.
Wrong. The cord has three vessels.
Correct. The vein brings oxygenated blood to the fetus.

questions.q: Which vessel carries oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus?

options.e: Wrong. Carries deoxygenated blood from the fetus.
Wrong. A shunt from the pulmonary artery to the aorta.
Wrong. A shunt that bypasses the liver.
Correct. Only the umbilical vein is oxygenated.

questions.q: Which fetal shunt bypasses the liver?

options.e: Correct. It opens into the IVC.

questions.q: Which shunt carries oxygen-rich blood from the right atrium to the left atrium?

options.e: Wrong. It joins the pulmonary artery to the descending aorta.

questions.q: Which shunt carries blood from the pulmonary artery to the descending aorta?

options.e: Wrong. This is the postnatal remnant.

questions.q: Which two shunts bypass the lungs?

options.e: Wrong. The ductus venosus bypasses the liver.
Correct. Both bypass the non-functional lungs.
Wrong. The ductus venosus bypasses the liver.
Wrong. The foramen ovale also bypasses the lungs.

questions.q: Why is fetal pulmonary vascular resistance high?

options.e: Wrong. The fetal PO2 is low.
Wrong. The placenta has low resistance.

options.t: Low O2 causes hypoxic vasoconstriction in collapsed, fluid-filled lungs

questions.q: Which statement about fetal vascular resistance is correct?

options.e: Correct. SVR is low because it includes the placenta.
Wrong. This is the adult pattern.

questions.q: Why is fetal systemic vascular resistance low?

options.e: Wrong. It is open in fetal life.

options.t: The systemic circulation includes the low-resistance placenta
options.e: Correct. The placenta is a very low-resistance pathway.

questions.q: What is the fetal PO2 range?

options.e: Correct. The placenta is not very effective at gas exchange.

questions.q: How does HbF affect the O2 dissociation curve?

options.t: It shifts it to the right
It shifts it to the left
options.e: Correct. HbF has high O2 affinity.

questions.q: Compared with adult blood, fetal blood has about how much more hemoglobin?

options.e: Correct. Higher Hb increases O2 carrying capacity.

questions.q: Which describes the fetal circulation compared with the infant?

options.e: Wrong. Fetal shunting is right to left.
Correct. The infant is high pressure with left-to-right flow.

questions.q: Why are the fetal lungs kept deflated?

options.t: To prevent filling with fluid and meconium debris
options.e: Correct. No air exists in amniotic fluid so there is no breathing.

questions.q: When are spinal and brain stem reflexes present?

options.e: Correct. The cerebral cortex is still immature.

questions.q: When is meconium formed?

options.e: Correct. It forms in the late GIT.
Wrong. It is formed before birth.

questions.q: When does the fetal kidney start producing urine and at what rate?

options.e: Correct. Fetal urine contributes 70-80% of amniotic fluid.

questions.q: Which organ controls fluid and electrolyte balance in the fetus?

options.e: Wrong. It depends on the placenta.
Correct. The fetal kidney does not control it.

questions.q: What is the sole source of energy for the fetus?

options.e: Correct. Glucose is the fetal fuel.

questions.q: In which period of pregnancy is fetal bone ossification and weight gain rapid, with active calcium and phosphate metabolism?

options.e: Wrong. This is the embryonic period.
Correct. Calcium and phosphate metabolism is active from week 12 to 40.
